title: Selected classical commentary, separate from the Gemara reconstruction

sources.author: Rashi
sources.ref: Rashi on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. יאוש שלא מדעת
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: דבר שסתמו יאוש לכשידע שנפל ממנו וכשמצאו עדיין לא ידעו הבעלים שנפל מהן:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body. Defines the disputed timing; it does not itself endorse either disputant.

sources.author: Rashi
sources.ref: Rashi on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. מהשתא הוי יאוש
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: שהרי נפל וכשיודע שוב אין דעתו עליו:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body explaining Rava’s position, not an independent ruling by Rashi.

sources.author: Tosafot
sources.ref: Tosafot on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. דלכי נפל מיניה לא מיאש
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: ואע"ג דהשתא מיאש אקראי בעלמא הוא ומתחילה לא היה עומד ליאש:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body. The identifying-mark context comes from the Gemara immediately above; this is a qualification, not a dispute with Rashi.

sources.author: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet)
sources.ref: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet) on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. ורבא אמר הוי יאוש כיון דלכי ידע לא סגי דלא מייאש
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: וכל היכא דאמרינן דיאוש שלא מדעת לא הוי יאוש או בדבר שאין בו סימן לאביי או בדבר שיש בו סימן לכולי עלמא אף על גב דאייאש לבסוף לא מהני ואפילו למאן דאמר בעלמא דיאוש כדי (לא קשיא) שאני הכא שנטלה בתורת גזל וכיון שבשעת נטילה לא זכה הרי ידו כיד הבעלים וכנפקד שלהם שאין יאוש מועיל בו והיינו דאמרינן לעיל דכי אתי באיסורא אתא לידיה ולאו באיסורא ממש שהרי לא נתכוון לגזול וחייב הוא ליטלה כיון שיש בה סימן אלא בשעת איסורא קאמרינן כלומר דכי אתא לידיה ברשות בעלים קיימא וכנוטל מידם דמי וזה ברור.
sources.context: Continuous excerpt within the paragraph attributed to הריטב״א at its close in Shittah Mekubbetzet. Transcription including its parenthesis preserved. Not checked against a standalone Ritva edition. The marked-item duty to pick up must not be generalized to every unmarked object.

sources.author: Rashi
sources.ref: Rashi on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. עשוי למשמש
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: וקודם שמצאו זה נודע לבעלים שנפלו ונואשו:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body on habitual purse checking in the scattered-coins reply (Gemara 21b:7).

sources.author: Rashi
sources.ref: Rashi on Bava Metzia 22b, s.v. ואיסורא דומיא דהיתירא
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: כיון דמחד קרא ילפינן מצויה אצל כל אדם שיחזור ושאינה מצויה יזכה בה איתקושי אתקוש להדדי זו לאיסורא וזו להיתירא:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body explaining the warrant for the Gemara’s final comparison (22b:6).

sources.author: Rashi
sources.ref: Rashi on Bava Metzia 22b, s.v. אף איסורא
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: דמצויה אצל כל אדם לא חילק בין אין סימן דכי ידע מיאש ליש סימן דלכי ידע לא מיאש וכי היכי דיש סימן אסירא כי אין סימן נמי אסירא היכא דאיכא למימר לא ידע דנפלה קודם שבאת ליד זה:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body. Preserve the awareness-before-pickup qualification; not a prohibition on all unmarked finds.

sources.author: Tosafot
sources.ref: Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22b, s.v. איסורא דומיא דהתירא
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: מה שמתיר אבודה ממנו ומכל אדם ע"כ לא איצטריך קרא בידע ומתיאש דהא אפילו במצויין אצל כל אדם מותרת ביאוש אלא לא אצטריך אלא כי לא ידע ואע"ג דלכי ידע לא מתיאש אפי' אם יש בו סימן כיון שהיא אבודה מכל אדם ה"נ איסורא דהיינו מצוייה אצל כל אדם דאסור כה"ג דלא ידעינן דמיאש בין יש בו סימן בין שאין בו סימן ואין להתיר אלא דמיאש קודם דאתא לידיה דשריא רחמנא:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body. Splitting its redundancy argument and comparison into nodes is editorial; they are one commentary, not independent proofs.

sources.author: Tosafot
sources.ref: Tosafot on Bava Metzia 22b, s.v. תיובתא דרבא
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: רבא ידע שפיר הך ברייתא כדמשמע קצת לעיל (דף כא:) דקאמר בזוטו של ים כ"ע לא פליגי דשרי כדבעינן למימר לקמן אלא דלא דייק איסורא דומיא דהתירא:
sources.context: Complete dibbur body. Explains Rava’s awareness of the source and failure to draw this comparison; not another refutation.

sources.author: Rashba
sources.ref: Rashba on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. זוטו של ים ושלוליתו של נהר … רחמנא אפקריה
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: מסתברא דהפקר גמור הוא, ואפילו מרדף אחריהם, ואפילו אמר בפירוש לא מיאשנא, אפילו הכי שריא דרחמנא אפקריה.
sources.context: Opening sentence excerpt. The omitted discussion tests Biran River and sand cases; a second separate excerpt below preserves the recoverability boundary. This is Rashba’s analysis of the exceptional category, not psychological despair.

sources.author: Rashba
sources.ref: Rashba on Bava Metzia 21b, s.v. זוטו של ים ושלוליתו של נהר … רחמנא אפקריה (recoverability)
sources.license: Classical Hebrew public domain; digital edition attribution retained under CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.text: אבל לאו כזוטו של ים הוא לגמרי, משום דהא אפשר לארבולי וזמנין דמשכח ליה, והילכך כל היכא דשמעינן דלא אייאש, לא הוה ליה כזוטו של ים, ומחייב לאהדורי, אבל זוטו של ים, אבודה היא לגמרי, ומשעת נפילתו הויא הפקר גמור, כך נראה לי.
sources.context: Continuous closing excerpt about sifting sand, contrasted with complete loss. Earlier in the same dibbur Rashba also distinguishes recoverable Biran River; those later Gemara cases are contextual limits, not added base episodes.

nodes.speaker: Rashi
nodes.label: Rashi: the time of discovery
nodes.text: At discovery the owner is unaware, although learning of the loss would normally bring despair.

nodes.speaker: Rashi
nodes.label: Rashi: explaining Rava
nodes.text: Rava counts the response now: once the owner learns, the lost object will no longer occupy the owner’s concern.
nodes.note: An explanation of Rava’s position; do not turn it into Rashi’s own ruling.

nodes.speaker: Tosafot
nodes.label: Tosafot: marked loss is different
nodes.text: Later despair over a marked object is contingent; initially the owner was not standing ready to despair.
nodes.note: The Gemara supplies the identifying mark and expected recovery. Tosafot qualifies an overbroad extension of Rava, without attacking Rashi.

nodes.speaker: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet)
nodes.label: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet): possession for the owner
nodes.text: Where unnoticed despair is ineffective, pickup leaves the finder’s hand like the owner’s hand, as a custodian.

nodes.speaker: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet)
nodes.label: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet): later despair cannot cure it
nodes.text: Because the finder did not acquire at pickup and holds for the owner, the owner’s later despair does not confer acquisition.

nodes.speaker: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet)
nodes.label: Ritva (via Shittah Mekubbetzet): not necessarily theft
nodes.text: Ba-issura here describes taking while the object remains in the owner’s domain; it need not mean an intention to steal.
nodes.note: Ritva adds that a marked object must be picked up. No general duty concerning all unmarked finds is asserted here.

nodes.speaker: Editorial
nodes.label: Supplied: two distinct qualifications
nodes.text: Keep anticipated despair separate from contingent later despair, and ask whether pickup already made the finder a holder for the owner.

nodes.speaker: Rashi
nodes.label: Rashi: awareness precedes finding
nodes.text: The owner learned that the coins fell and despaired before this finder discovered them.

nodes.speaker: Editorial
nodes.label: Supplied: locate the changed premise
nodes.text: Read habitual checking through Rashi’s timing: the reply replaces the challenge’s assumption that the owner was still unaware.

nodes.speaker: Editorial
nodes.label: Supplied: retain the original target
nodes.text: This explains the base relation C6 attacking C2. It leaves the Mishnah intact and supplies no new refutation of Abaye.
nodes.note: No Tosafot coins node is added: ת״ש המוצא מעות כו׳ concerns the later public-place baraita, outside the selected scattered-coins exchange.

nodes.speaker: Rashi
nodes.label: Rashi: the same verse
nodes.text: Ordinary return and exceptional acquisition come from one verse, warranting their comparison.

nodes.speaker: Rashi
nodes.label: Rashi: the timing limit
nodes.text: Ordinary unmarked loss is prohibited here when the owner may not have learned of the loss before the finder took it.

nodes.speaker: Tosafot
nodes.label: Tosafot: why a special verse?
nodes.text: Known despair already permits ordinary loss. A river verse confined to that case would add nothing.

nodes.speaker: Tosafot
nodes.label: Tosafot: what the exception adds
nodes.text: The river permission therefore reaches lack of awareness, even with a mark and even where learning would not produce despair.

nodes.speaker: Tosafot
nodes.label: Tosafot: carry across the comparison
nodes.text: The ordinary prohibition likewise covers absence of known despair, with or without a mark; prior despair before pickup remains the route to permission.

nodes.speaker: Editorial
nodes.label: Supplied: make the extra premise visible
nodes.text: Join the same-verse comparison to Tosafot’s redundancy reasoning and preserve Rashi’s timing limit. River permission alone is insufficient.

nodes.speaker: Tosafot
nodes.label: Tosafot: Rava knew the baraita
nodes.text: Rava knew the river source but had not drawn the prohibition–permission comparison. This explains the refutation, rather than adding a proof.
nodes.note: Kept disconnected as an explanatory note, not another premise proving the conclusion.

nodes.speaker: Rashba
nodes.label: Rashba: scriptural ownerlessness
nodes.text: True loss to everyone is complete ownerlessness by the Torah, even if the owner pursues it and expressly refuses to despair.

nodes.speaker: Rashba
nodes.label: Rashba: recoverability matters
nodes.text: Siftable sand can still yield the object. On hearing that its owner has not despaired, return is required; it is not fully like loss to everyone.

nodes.speaker: Editorial
nodes.label: Supplied: keep the exceptional scope
nodes.text: Rashba sharpens the base scope note: psychological despair does not create this exceptional permission, and a river location alone does not establish it.

nodes.speaker: Editorial
nodes.label: Supplied: do not replace the comparison
nodes.text: This account limits which losses enter the exceptional category. It does not by itself prove the ordinary unawareness prohibition in the final river map.

views.name: Opening · Rashi / Tosafot / Ritva
views.title: Timing, expectation, possession.
views.intro: Rashi defines the timing and explains Rava. Tosafot qualifies the marked-object case. Ritva, quoted in Shittah Mekubbetzet, explains why later despair cannot repair pickup for the owner.
views.note: C = attributed commentary; R = our supplied synthesis. These are complementary explanations and qualifications, not an invented dispute. Base context: O1–O2, O4–O7.

views.name: Coins · Rashi
views.title: Awareness before discovery.
views.intro: Rashi supplies a precise temporal reading of the purse-checking reply. Our two supplied nodes locate its effect in the unchanged coins map.
views.note: KC2–KC3 are our mapping explanation. The actual attack C6 → C2 remains in the base map; no second attack or undercut is introduced here.

views.name: River · Rashi / Tosafot
views.title: Why does the comparison work?
views.intro: Rashi states the same-verse warrant and awareness qualification. Tosafot supplies the redundancy argument that explains what the exceptional permission adds.
views.note: KR6 is an editorial synthesis of Rashi and Tosafot, now split into two numbered inference steps. KR7 remains an isolated explanation of what Rava missed. The final 22b comparison is distinct from the earlier 22a river exchange.

views.name: River boundary · Rashba
views.title: Loss to everyone is a real limit.
views.intro: Rashba distinguishes scriptural ownerlessness from the owner’s psychological despair. His recoverability cases clarify the opening exception used in the final comparison.
views.note: The Biran River and sand discussions are commentary context, not newly encoded Gemara episodes. This selected account does not survey all opinions on the exception.
